# 1 Samuel Chapter 27 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 166r–166v | **Source Image:** 1SA_027_page_001.jpg

---

**1** David thought to himself, "One of these days Saul is going to kill me. The best thing I can do is escape to Philistine territory. Then Saul will give up searching for me anywhere in Israel, and I'll be out of his reach."

**2** So David crossed over with his six hundred men to Achish son of Maoch, king of Gath.

**3** David settled in Gath with Achish — he and his men, each with their families. David had his two wives with him: Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail, Nabal's widow from Carmel.

**4** When Saul was told that David had fled to Gath, he stopped looking for him.

**5** David said to Achish, "If you're willing, give me a place in one of the outlying towns to live in. Why should your servant live in the royal city with you?"

**6** So Achish gave him Ziklag that day. That is why Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah ever since.

**7** David lived in Philistine territory for a year and four months.

**8** During that time, David and his men raided the Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites — peoples who had long inhabited the region stretching toward Shur and Egypt.

**9** Whenever David attacked an area, he left no one alive — man or woman — but took the sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, and clothing. Then he would return to Achish.

**10** When Achish asked, "Where did you raid today?" David would say, "The Negev of Judah," or "The Negev of the Jerahmeelites," or "The Negev of the Kenites."

**11** David left no survivors who could report to Gath, thinking, "They might talk and expose us." This was his practice the entire time he lived in Philistine territory.

**12** Achish trusted David completely. He thought, "David has made himself so hated among his own people that he'll be my servant forever."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

1. **27:1 — David's despair**: After two dramatic encounters with Saul, two covenant renewals, two repentances — David gives up. "One of these days Saul is going to kill me." The man who consulted God through the ephod in chapter 23 now consults only his own fear. The text records no prayer, no oracle. David acts alone.

2. **27:9-11 — the moral abyss**: This is the darkest chapter in David's story. He conducts raids of total annihilation — leaving no witnesses — and systematically lies to his patron about whom he's attacking. The narrator offers no commentary, no justification, no divine approval. The silence is the point.

3. **27:12 — "forever"**: Achish's conclusion is triply ironic. David will not serve him forever — within months, the Philistine lords will refuse David's presence in their army (ch. 29), and within a year, David will be anointed king of Judah. Achish has been completely deceived, and the reader knows it.

— PNEUMA
